_note: What Fumi, who keeps the Hanami teahouse in Sakurazaka, says when the farmer talks to her (Talk, README.md, Villagers): the first pick whose if holds names the lines, one of them by the day; gift_ lines answer a gift by its reaction (gift_birthday on her birthday, spring 26), gift_items her own answers to a keepsake and to dishes. The close lines from band 4, after_tea once her band 5 scene is seen (heart_fumi_5). Our own lines.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I shut the teahouse for this. Someone else's dango, for once, and I just sit and eat it.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Shaved ice! At home I'd never let myself. Tonight doesn't count.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The moon looks the same from the teahouse, but it's better with company.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Before anyone's awake tomorrow I'll rake the gravel. A clean start, my mother called it.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Back again? Sit, sit. The second cup is always the better one.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I'm only watching the kettle. It never boils while I talk, you know.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Welcome to the Hanami teahouse. I'm Fumi. My mother poured tea here, and her mother before.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Miners stop on the way up, Ichiro on the way back. Everyone tells me everything. Funny, that.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Rain on the cherry trees, steam off the cups. A slow day, but I like the sound of it.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The cherries along the road! People walk up from the village just to stand under them.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: When a petal lands in your cup, you have to drink it. That's the rule here.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Warabi mochi and cold barley tea in summer. The creek keeps them cooler than any icebox.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The leaves go red all the way up to the mine. Ichiro says the woods smell like smoke and apples.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Snow on the bridge. Walk the middle of the planks, the edges are ice.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The stone lanterns by the bridge? My grandfather set them, so nobody walks into the creek at night.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Ichiro eats lunch on my gravel every day and never once sits on the bench. Stubborn man.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Butterbur buds come up on both banks of the creek, above the bridge. Bitter, but with a little miso they're spring in one bite.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Myoga grows on the creek bank upstream of the bridge. I slice it thin over cold tofu. It's the taste of my summer menu.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Chestnuts drop by the pines up behind the teahouse. I roast a pan of them for the counter, and nobody leaves before it's empty.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Winter's bare here. Ichiro says there's enoki by the far pine past his grove. I'll take his word. I don't walk in the snow.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: You know what today is? The last cherries always fall on my birthday. I shut early to watch them go.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: For my birthday? Oh... I pour for everyone all year, and nobody ever pours for me. Thank you.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Your cup's ready. I saw you on the road and put the kettle on. Don't look so surprised.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The miners get the chipped cups. You get my mother's. That's how it is now.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I tried your turnips in miso this week. Ichiro had three bowls and said nothing, which is his highest praise.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The tea merchant wrote again. I used his letter to light the stove. It burned very nicely.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I've started writing my mother's recipes down. Someone should have them, after me. Someone who'll come by.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Oh, how lovely! This goes on the counter for everyone to see. Well, after I've had some.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: For me? You're kind. I'll have it with my afternoon cup.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Thank you. I'll find a place for it.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Fish, in a teahouse? The cups will smell of it for a week.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: A rock. In my teahouse. Please take it outside.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: No more today, or I'll have to give you free tea forever.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: A wind chime! I'll hang it over the counter. Every breeze will tell me someone's coming.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: This would sell out by noon if I put it on my menu. May I copy it?

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Home cooking! A teahouse keeper never gets anyone's but her own. Thank you.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Oh, a dish. I'll have it for supper, thank you.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Ah... a fish dish. I'm sure Ichiro will love it.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Mother's kettle pours slower than mine, but sweeter. Come and taste the difference.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I've kept you a cup on the back shelf. Nobody else drinks from it. Don't tell anyone.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The road looks different on days you come by. Brighter. That's not the tea talking.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Tome has me sewing cushions for the shrine. Three days, she says, and not a minute more.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The tea merchant sent a letter. I wrote back that I'm getting married. He hasn't answered.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Good morning. The first cup is on the kotatsu. Mother's kettle, as promised.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Take a rice ball for the field. You forget to eat when the weather's good.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I can hear the hens from here. They wake earlier than any teahouse keeper.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Welcome home. Last cup of the day. Sit, before it goes cold.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Ichiro asked if I'd still pour his lunch. As if I'd let anyone else do it badly.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The farm is quieter than the road at night. I like it. I can hear the kettle think.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I watered your dry plots this morning, before the first tea. Tell me if I drowned anything.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: The rows by the path were parched, so I gave them a can. You owe me a cup for that.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I topped up the coop's feed box this morning. The hens greeted me like an old friend.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: I put feed in the coop before breakfast. Next time, you can carry the sack yourself.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Customers ask how married life is. I tell them the tea tastes the same and the walk home is better.

lines.speaker: fumi
lines.text: Sit for one cup? You don't have to pay anymore. That's the only drawback of marrying me.
